heading: PPF for Minors: Can Parents Invest ₹3 Lakh Annually?
tldr: The Public Provident Fund (PPF) has an annual contribution limit of ₹1.5 lakh per financial year across all accounts held by an individual.
This ₹1.5 lakh limit applies to the combined contributions made by parents into their minor child's PPF account.
If both parents contribute ₹1.5 lakh each, the total of ₹3 lakh will exceed the maximum permissible limit for the child's account.
Any amount contributed above ₹1.5 lakh in a minor's PPF account will not earn interest and will not be eligible for tax benefits under Section 80C.
Contributions to a minor's PPF account are clubbed with the income of the parent (usually the higher-earning parent) for income tax purposes.
caption:
Thinking of opening a PPF for your child? Many parents wonder if they can put ₹1.5 lakh each, totaling ₹3 lakh, into their child's account. The simple answer is no. You can only put a maximum of ₹1.5 lakh per year into a minor's PPF account, no matter who contributes. Amounts above this limit won't earn interest or give tax benefits.
